sections.h2: Which offices value property and collect tax in Graves County, KY?
sections.html:
Two county offices share the work in Graves County, with a third stepping in later. The PVA appraises land and buildings. The county's own PVA page adds that its staff does not set rates and does not take payments. Payments belong at the sheriff's counter, and a bill left unpaid past mid-April is turned over to the County Clerk.

Both the PVA and the Clerk operate from 1102 Paris Road in Mayfield, the PVA in Suite 2 at (270) 247-3301 and the Clerk in Suite 5, where the delinquent real estate tax line is (270) 247-1697. Each office lists its hours as eight to four-thirty. The sheriff keeps the same schedule on Central Time and accepts mailed checks, walk-in payments and online card payments. Cash, check and card are all taken at the counter. The sheriff cannot edit a bill's mailing address, because the PVA keeps that record.

Parcel data can be searched on the qPublic site that the sheriff's tax page recommends for Graves County records.

sections.h2: When do Graves County tax bills go out, and what if one never arrives?
sections.html:
The sheriff starts taking payment on October 1 of the assessment year. If your bill has not turned up by October 10, request a duplicate, which you can collect at the sheriff's office or print from its website.

Bill addresses come from the PVA, not the sheriff. Anything changed after June misses the tax roll for that year, so a seller who moved over the summer may find the bill sitting at the old mailbox.

KRS 134.015 supplies the discount and penalty steps used everywhere in the state. Pay in full by November 1 and keep two percent. The bill sits at face value through the end of the year. January adds five percent, and later payments add ten. The January 1 owner is personally liable for that year's tax, so a buyer who closes in July or October should put the sharing arrangement on paper.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Graves County assessment?
sections.html:
Nothing can be filed until you have talked with the PVA's staff. Kentucky's calendar puts the roll on public display for 13 days beginning in early May.

  • Ask for a PVA conference in or before that display window, and bring questions about how the number was built.
  • Get the appeal form to the Clerk's counter before it closes on the first workday after the display.
  • Assemble comparables, listings, photos of defects, insurance papers and building costs.
  • Make your case to the local appeals board, which sits about a month after the display and explains any change it makes.

Taxpayers may record the hearing on audio. A no-show after filing closes the door on the Kentucky Claims Commission.

sections.h2: What does the homestead exemption save a Graves County owner?
sections.html:
People who have turned 65, and people who are totally disabled, can knock $49,100 off the assessment for 2025-2026. For a house valued at the Census median, $147,800, that leaves $98,700 subject to tax.

The county's PVA page explains that exemptions are never granted on their own. Paperwork goes to the PVA first. Disabled applicants need to have been drawing disability benefits for the entire assessment period, and most must reapply every year.

The deduction follows the resident owner, so a buyer who qualifies files a fresh application.

sections.h2: What happens to a Graves County tax bill after April 15?
sections.html:
At the close of April 15, the sheriff passes every unpaid bill to the County Clerk. The paper becomes a certificate of delinquency, and the Clerk records a lien on the parcel. The sheriff's page states that prior-year taxes cannot be collected there after the transfer.

Notice and sale steps after transfer on a regular schedule (source: Kentucky Department of Revenue)
StepTiming
First attorney notice mailedWithin a month of transfer
Second notice naming the sale date20 or more days later, and inside 60 days
Published list of delinquent bills30 to 45 days ahead of the sale
Public saleBetween day 90 and day 135

From the day of transfer, one percent a month accrues, and the Clerk and the county attorney each take a commission. Using the state's sample, a $1,000 bill becomes $1,254 at transfer and $1,387.79 when paid inside five business days. After the sale, a third-party certificate holder collects instead of the county.

sections.h2: How should I handle taxes at a Graves County closing?
sections.html:
Say in the contract who pays the current year's bill. Dividing the year between seller and buyer is a private matter, since the sheriff bills only the January 1 owner. Ask the sheriff or Clerk for a payoff ahead of closing.

  • Ask the Clerk's delinquent line whether any earlier year is open, since that lien outlasts the sale.
  • Include the buyer's in-care-of address in the deed, which KRS 382.135 demands.
  • Confirm owner name and acreage on the qPublic record against the deed.

The deed also triggers a transfer tax payable by the seller; the Graves County Clerk page on this site walks through it.

sections.h2: How did the 2021 tornado affect Mayfield and Graves County?
sections.html:
On December 10, 2021, a long-track tornado went through the county and caused widespread damage in Mayfield. The Graves County Courthouse was among the buildings hit hard. Owners rebuilding or clearing a lot should ask the PVA how destroyed or rebuilt structures are valued as of each January 1.

Cash purchasers do buy storm-damaged or half-finished houses as they stand, and the new deed is still filed at the Clerk's office on Paris Road.

sections.h2: What is the Graves County housing market like?
sections.html:
Graves County covers 552 square miles of land at the state's southwestern edge, in the Jackson Purchase, and borders McCracken, Marshall, Calloway, Carlisle and Hickman counties plus two Tennessee counties. It forms the Mayfield micropolitan area, which belongs to the Paducah-Mayfield combined statistical area. It was formed in 1824. Mayfield is the county seat, with Wingo the only other city, and part of the Clarks River National Wildlife Refuge sits inside the lines. Dark-fired tobacco and a woolen mill with clothing makers shaped the early economy, and the county was caught up in the Black Patch Tobacco Wars. Alcohol rules are mixed: the county is limited dry, while Mayfield voters approved store sales in 2016.

  • 37,050 residents in 2025, up 1.1 percent from 2020.
  • 14,139 households and a 76.1 percent ownership rate.
  • Median home value of $147,800, against median gross rent of $775.
  • Median household income of $50,772, with 16.6 percent of residents in poverty.
  • A 56.2 percent labor force participation rate, and 83 new-home permits for 2025.

With so few permits against more than 14,000 households, most sales here are resales, and clear title and condition matter to buyers.

faqs.q: Where do Graves County property taxes get paid?
faqs.a: The Graves County Sheriff's Office handles current-year bills by mail, at the counter and online. Once April 15 has passed, the County Clerk handles whatever is open.

faqs.q: What if my Graves County tax bill did not come in the mail?
faqs.a: Request a duplicate from the sheriff if nothing has arrived by October 10. Addresses come from the PVA, and changes made after June are left out of that year's bills.

faqs.q: Does the Graves County homestead exemption apply on its own?
faqs.a: No. A written application to the PVA comes first, at (270) 247-3301, and the $49,100 deduction follows only for owners who have turned 65 or are totally disabled.

faqs.q: When does a Graves County bill move to the County Clerk?
faqs.a: On April 15, at closing time. The Clerk records a lien, the bill is relabeled a certificate of delinquency, and interest starts at one percent monthly.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Graves County house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer's title company pays the lien out of the proceeds, so call the Clerk's delinquent line at (270) 247-1697 for the figure.
